Jacques is a chef. He claims that 90% of his customers are satisfied with his cooking. Marie suspects
that the true percentage is lower than 90%. She asks a random sample of 15 of Jacques’ customers
whether they are satisfied. She then performs a hypothesis test of the null hypothesis p = 0.9 against
the alternative hypothesis p < 0.9, where p is the population proportion of customers who are satisfied.
She decides to reject the null hypothesis if fewer than 12 customers are satisfied.
